comments.note: AppCountryISOsParam.getCountries() and AppCountryIDsParam.getCountries() both obtain a fresh AppFactory::createCountries() collection per call inside a loop. This is a minor inefficiency — assigning the collection to a local variable before the loop (as done in AppCountryIDsParam already) avoids repeated factory look-ups. AppCountryISOsParam already follows this pattern correctly; no action needed.

AppCountryIDsParam declares PARAM_COUNTRY_IDS and AppCountryISOsParam declares PARAM_COUNTRY_ISOS locally because AppCountriesAPIInterface does not yet exist. Once the interface is introduced in a later WP, these duplicates should be resolved by referencing the canonical interface constants (tracked in Params/README.md).

AppCountryISOsHandler imports Application_Countries_Country but never uses it directly — the type appears only in the return-type doc comment of resolveValueFromSubject(). This matches the identical pattern in AppCountryIDsHandler, so it is consistent. A future cleanup could remove the unused import and rely purely on the phpdoc, or keep it for IDE navigability (current approach is fine).

AppCountryISOsParam.getCountries() calls AppFactory::createCountries() once outside the loop — this is correct and efficient. Pattern is consistent with AppCountryIDsParam. No action needed.

AppCountryISOsValidation — if an ISO value in the list is non-string (e.g. an integer slipped through), the (string) cast silently converts it. This is consistent with AppCountryIDsValidation's (int) cast pattern and is acceptable given StringListParameter already filters non-string entries upstream.

getCountries() calls getByISO() which throws CountryException if an ISO is unknown. Validation runs before getCountries() in normal API flow, so this is only a risk if validation is bypassed or selectValue() is called with an unvalidated ISO. Same risk exists in AppCountryIDsParam — consistent but worth noting for future hardening.

isoExists() delegates to CountryCollection.filterCode() which lowercases the input, so case-insensitivity advertised in the param description is correctly handled at the collection level — not the param/validation level. No action needed.
